clue.text: Press uniform when going on guard

blocks.note: to ward is to guard or protect, as in ward off
a robe is official dress, a kind of uniform for judges or clergy

explanation.surface: A tailor presses a soldier's uniform before he goes on guard duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like a verb for ironing, but it is a noun: an old word for a clothes cupboard. 'going on' places the uniform after the guard.
explanation.definitionFit: A press is an old word for a tall cupboard where clothes are kept, which is exactly what a wardrobe is.

clue.text: Into battle with the Lancers?

blocks.note: surface reading: charging with a cavalry regiment armed with lances
setter's reading: the Lancers is a nineteenth-century square dance, a set of quadrilles

explanation.walkthrough: The Lancers is both a cavalry regiment and an old ballroom dance, so a dance performed before going into battle fits both.
explanation.definitionFit: A war dance is a ceremonial dance performed before battle to rouse warriors, combining fighting and dancing.

clue.text: Remember to go round with the hat again?

definitions.text: to go round with the hat again

blocks.note: first meaning: call back to mind

blocks.clueFragment: to go round with the hat again
blocks.note: second meaning: to collect money a second time

explanation.walkthrough: Going round with the hat is passing it for donations; doing it again is to re-collect.
explanation.definitionFit: To recollect something is to bring it back to mind, which is to remember it.

clue.text: Figure in a trilby or homburg

indicators.note: in tells you the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: surface padding: the first hat sets the scene and holds no letters
the letters run across the end of or into the start of homburg

explanation.surface: A man cuts a fine figure in his felt hat, a trilby or a homburg.
explanation.walkthrough: Trilby and homburg are both styles of men's felt hat, so 'Figure' looks like the wearer's appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhomb, or rhombus, is a geometric figure: a parallelogram with four equal sides.

clue.text: "The Complacent American" -- what a novel title!

blocks.note: first meaning: a smug, conformist businessman, a term from the novel's hero
second meaning: the 1922 novel by Sinclair Lewis about George F ...

explanation.walkthrough: 'what a novel title!' sounds like praise for an original name, but it literally means the title of a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinclair Lewis's character became a byword, so a babbitt is any self-satisfied, materialistic middle-class American.

clue.text: Sulphur -- look at this sample

blocks.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
to watch something is to look at it

explanation.surface: A chemist examines a yellow sample of sulphur.
explanation.definitionFit: A swatch is a small piece of fabric or material shown as a specimen, so it is a sample.

clue.text: Hat that guarantees there are no flies on its wearer?

definitions.text: that guarantees there are no flies on its wearer?

blocks.note: first meaning: a soft felt hat with a broad brim

blocks.clueFragment: that guarantees there are no flies on its wearer?
blocks.note: second meaning: 'no flies on him' means he is alert and sharp

explanation.walkthrough: A broad-brimmed hat might literally keep flies off; the idiom 'no flies on someone' means they are shrewd.
explanation.definitionFit: A wideawake is a low-crowned felt hat with a wide brim, and someone wide awake is fully alert.

clue.text: Military band in parade

blocks.note: first meaning: a unit of soldiers, especially cavalry
second meaning: to march in procession

explanation.walkthrough: 'Military band' suggests musicians, but band here is a group of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a cavalry or artillery unit, and to troop is to march in order, as at Trooping the Colour.

clue.text: Drive girl up in an hour

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top
in tells you the girl's name sits inside the hour

blocks.note: HR is the abbreviation for hour
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is driven up to town in an hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' looks like motoring with the girl, but it is the definition, as in driving a nail; 'up' turns the name round because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive a nail is to hammer it in, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: A reminder to one proceeding slowly

blocks.note: first meaning: something that jogs the memory
second meaning: a person running at a gentle trot

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a reminder sent to someone slow; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A jogger is anything that jogs the memory, and also a person who runs at an easy, unhurried pace.

clue.text: Clergyman off with redhead -- see front page

indicators.note: off with means take away, so the clergyman loses something

blocks.note: a rector is a parish priest in the Church of England
the head, meaning first letter, of the word red

explanation.surface: A cleric goes off with a red-haired woman, a story fit for the front page of a tabloid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redhead' looks like a ginger companion, but it is split: red's head is its first letter, R, which is removed from RECTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, the recto is the right-hand page of an open book, the side that faces you first.

clue.text: Sort of carpet Leopold and Dora ordered inside

indicators.note: ordered means arranged afresh, so the letters of the name Dora are rearranged
inside tells you one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: Leopold Bloom is the hero of James Joyce's novel Ulysses
the letters of Dora rearranged

explanation.surface: Leopold and Dora choose a carpet and order it for their home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' seems to mean they bought the carpet, but it is the rearranging signal; Leopold is not a first name to use but Joyce's hero, known by his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadloom is carpet woven in one wide piece on a broad loom, so it is a kind of carpet.

clue.text: Making up to fill in time

definitions.text: Making up to fill in time

blocks.note: surface reading: putting on make-up, or making a time sheet up
setter's reading: inventing words on the spot to cover a gap in a performance

explanation.walkthrough: 'Making up' suggests cosmetics or compensation; here it means improvising, as a performer does when something goes wrong on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad-libbing is speaking without a script, inventing words on the spot, often to cover a pause or delay.

clue.text: Its downfall was observed by 20

blocks.note: surface reading: the ruin or fall from power of some person or regime
setter's reading: 20 is Isaac Newton, who by legend watched a fruit fall from a tree

explanation.walkthrough: 20 is NEWTON; the story goes that a fruit falling in his orchard set him thinking about gravity.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says Newton saw an apple drop from a tree, and its fall inspired his theory of gravitation.

clue.text: Drugs dealer exposed in letters to Church Times

indicators.note: the words that follow are laid out letter by letter in a new arrangement

blocks.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drug dealer is exposed in letters written to the Church Times, a British Anglican weekly newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Church Times is a real newspaper, which disguises the split into an abbreviation plus a word, all seven letters then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemist is the British word for a pharmacist, who sells medicines, so in a joking way a drugs dealer.

clue.text: Puck gets pushed around by the players in this entertainment

blocks.clueFragment: Puck gets pushed around by the players
blocks.note: surface reading: Shakespeare's mischievous sprite in A Midsummer Night's Dream bullied by actors
setter's reading: a rubber disc struck across the rink by sportsmen with sticks

explanation.walkthrough: Puck and 'players' point to Shakespeare's comedy; the puck is the disc used in a winter sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice hockey is a spectator sport, a form of entertainment, in which players drive a puck over ice.

clue.text: The cutter who follows the sewer

definitions.text: The cutter who follows the sewer

blocks.note: surface reading: a tailor's cutter working beside a seamstress
setter's reading: sewer is one who sows seed, and harvest comes after sowing

explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' reads as one who sews, or a drain; read it as sower, one who sows seed, and the cutter is the harvester who comes later.
explanation.definitionFit: A reaper cuts ripe corn at harvest, the work that follows the sowing of the seed in spring.

clue.text: Sin with young lad delivering goods

blocks.note: to err is to do wrong, to sin
and means together with
a boy is a young male

explanation.surface: A delivery lad is tempted into sin.
explanation.walkthrough: The word lad does double duty in feel only: young alone gives BOY, and the definition is the delivery lad as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand boy is a youth employed to run errands, such as carrying goods to customers.

clue.text: Flounder, perhaps, finding the horizontal angle

blocks.note: flat means level, horizontal
to angle is to fish with a rod and line

explanation.surface: Someone floundering tries to find the horizontal angle on a diagram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flounder' looks like a verb for struggling and 'angle' like geometry; both are fishing terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A flounder is one example of a flatfish, like plaice and sole, so 'perhaps' marks it as an example.

clue.text: The way an old character sounds in broadcast

indicators.note: sounds tells you to use how the character's name is said, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
a rune is a letter of an ancient Germanic alphabet

explanation.surface: An actor puts on an old-fashioned voice for a character in a radio broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like radio, but it is the definition in its farming sense of scattering seed widely.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcast as an adjective means scattered far and wide, like seed thrown by hand, which is what strewn means.

clue.text: Force that makes an amphibian get on

blocks.note: a newt is a small amphibian
on, taken from get on

explanation.surface: Some force is needed to make a sluggish amphibian get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' is not pressure here; it is the scientific unit of force named after Isaac Newton.
explanation.definitionFit: The newton is the SI unit of force, the force that accelerates one kilogram by one metre per second squared.

clue.text: We hear more than one of the lungs is involved

indicators.note: we hear means what follows is taken by its sound when spoken

blocks.note: plural describes more than one of something

explanation.surface: A doctor says that both lungs, not just one, are affected by the disease.
explanation.definitionFit: The pleura is the membrane around each lung, so pleural describes something belonging to the lungs.

clue.text: Small NCO up on hill as disciplinary officer

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: CORP is the short form of corporal, a non-commissioned officer
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A corporal stands on a hill keeping order as discipline officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' signals the shortened word CORP, which is reversed to PROC and placed on TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A proctor is a university official in Oxford and Cambridge responsible for student discipline.

clue.text: As much as any member, left or right, can take

definitions.text: As much as any member, left or right, can take

blocks.note: surface reading: a party member of either political wing

blocks.clueFragment: member, left or right, can take
blocks.note: setter's reading: a limb, either one, and what it can carry

explanation.walkthrough: 'left or right' suggests politics, but the member is a limb, either the left one or the right.
explanation.definitionFit: An armful is the quantity that can be held in one arm, a limb on either side of the body.

clue.text: Pie, say, giving us short commons

definitions.note: pie said out loud is pi, the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: commons are a shared allowance of food, a ration

explanation.surface: A pie is served out so meanly that it leaves everyone on short rations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short commons' is an idiom for meagre food, but here short is the cutting signal and commons is the ration; 'Pie, say' points to pi by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Pi, which sounds like pie, is the fixed ratio of any circle's circumference to its diameter, so it is an example.

clue.text: Whip hand at the outset grabbed by Chinese society

indicators.note: at the outset points to the very start of the word before it
something grabbed by another is held inside it

blocks.note: a tong is a Chinese secret society or guild
the first letter of hand

explanation.surface: A whip hand is held from the start by a powerful Chinese organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip hand' reads as an idiom for control; whip alone is the definition and hand is wordplay. A tong is a Chinese secret society or guild.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a narrow leather strip, used as the lash of a whip, or a whip itself.

clue.text: The   question that brings murderers to book

definitions.text: The   question that brings murderers to book

blocks.clueFragment: The   question that brings murderers to book
blocks.note: surface reading: a detective's question that leads to killers being punished
setter's reading: the question of who killed whom forms the plot of a whole novel

explanation.walkthrough: 'brings to book' means punish, but here the book is literal: the question of guilt is the whole plot of a detective novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A whodunnit is a detective story built around discovering which character committed the murder.

clue.text: Almost too hard to tear open

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is lost

blocks.note: fruit that is unripe is still too hard to eat

explanation.surface: A packet is almost too hard to tear open.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrip is an old verb meaning to rip open or cut apart, so it means to tear open.

clue.text: Military jacket of crack foot formation

indicators.note: a formation is an arrangement, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: An elite infantry unit parades in formation wearing smart regimental jackets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack foot formation' reads as a unit of elite foot soldiers, but formation is the signal to rearrange the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A frock coat is a long, knee-length coat, historically worn as part of military and formal dress.

clue.text: Duffer cut off by teacher

indicators.note: cut off means its end is chopped away

blocks.note: in British sporting slang a rabbit is a poor player, especially a weak batsman

explanation.surface: A hopeless pupil is stopped short by a teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbi literally means 'my master' and is the title of a Jewish religious teacher and scholar.

clue.text: Run scored off a side at cricket

definitions.text: Run scored off a side at cricket

blocks.note: surface reading: a run made against the opposing team
setter's reading: off the batsman's body, a ball deflecting off the leg, also one side of the field

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the off side and leg side are the two halves of the field; a run taken after the ball strikes the batter's body rather than the bat is credited to neither batter.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg bye is an extra run taken when the ball deflects off the batsman's leg or body instead of the bat.

clue.text: Series of religious pictures is bound to fold

blocks.note: surface reading: a sequence of church paintings
setter's reading: three hinged panels joined so that the outer wings close over the centre

explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to fold' sounds like certain failure; it means hinged together so the panels close like shutters.
explanation.definitionFit: A triptych is an altarpiece of three painted panels, often religious scenes, hinged so the side panels fold inward.
